from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 8  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [214, 173, 221, 132, 117]
    demands = [47, 39, 40, 33, 33, 54, 59, 55]
    cost_matrix = [[24.24, 8.05, 28.9, 29.33, 16.27, 16.34, 11.63, 6.4], [29.53, 9.45, 15.48, 12.47, 24.89, 20.86, 28.3, 24.07], [8.28, 6.68, 10.35, 20.37, 9.68, 3.14, 12.03, 22.05], [3.46, 13.49, 16.84, 23.74, 24.89, 20.99, 8.67, 9.85], [10.98, 13.38, 25.44, 21.39, 21.83, 3.45, 24.66, 29.18]]
    emission_matrix = [[13.38, 18.86, 4.58, 6.55, 13.36, 12.23, 10.68, 20.0], [6.84, 11.51, 15.91, 13.62, 12.68, 8.31, 2.79, 1.0], [6.28, 11.14, 14.57, 17.52, 12.69, 6.36, 3.82, 14.83], [15.31, 15.52, 5.03, 11.79, 14.37, 10.6, 7.92, 13.54], [7.85, 13.97, 13.34, 1.86, 2.02, 6.76, 7.94, 2.68]]
    fixed_costs = [[275, 81, 129, 83, 271, 217, 226, 83], [120, 92, 245, 174, 263, 195, 140, 290], [130, 287, 140, 110, 241, 64, 187, 205], [62, 197, 85, 79, 59, 123, 144, 129], [63, 298, 118, 177, 92, 294, 250, 218]]
    moq = [[11, 5, 20, 15, 10, 5, 14, 10], [18, 14, 18, 16, 14, 15, 10, 8], [19, 8, 10, 16, 16, 15, 14, 9], [6, 11, 15, 13, 9, 12, 7, 16], [18, 10, 14, 5, 17, 11, 5, 7]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: [Insert date]
Subject: Balancing Delivered Cost and CO2 Impact in Store Deliveries

Context
Our store delivery network must balance delivered cost with environmental impact. Each shipping lane carries both a dollar cost per unit and a CO2 emission rate per unit. In practice, the least-expensive lanes often have higher carbon intensity, while cleaner options can be more expensive. To support margin goals and sustainability commitments, we will evaluate shipping plans using a blended score that accounts for both cost and emissions.

Operational rules
To reflect how we actually run, the plan must adhere to the following:
- Route setup/activation: Starting any lane incurs a one-time setup outlay (carrier onboarding, contract fees, dock scheduling, and any paperwork). A lane is either active or not; once activated, the setup outlay is incurred in full regardless of shipped volume.
- Minimum order quantities: If a lane is activated, we must ship at least a defined minimum on that lane to justify equipment and dock time. Partial loads are not accepted for activated lanes.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can be served by no more than a set number of warehouses to manage receiving capacity and vendor complexity. This necessitates consolidation and discourages excessive fragmentation of inbound shipments.

Supply and demand
Warehouse shipments cannot exceed available inventory at each location. Each store has a required demand that must be met within the planning window. We will not propose plans that leave stores short or draw more product from a warehouse than it can supply.

Management priority
Leadership has set the relative importance of cost versus emissions. We will apply these weights to the variable shipping dollars per unit and the kg CO2 per unit. Setup outlays for activated lanes are added at full value and are not scaled by the weights. This blended evaluation ensures we fairly trade off cheaper but more polluting lanes against cleaner but higher-cost alternatives.

Business goal
We will determine which lanes to activate and how much to ship on each activated lane so that:
- Warehouse inventories are respected,
- Each store’s required demand is met,
- Activated lanes move at least their minimum order quantity,
- Each store is served by no more than the allowed number of warehouses, and
- The blended total—weighted variable shipping cost, weighted emissions, plus full setup outlays—is as low as possible under these rules.

This approach will produce a clear, actionable shipping plan that aligns with both financial targets and sustainability objectives. It will also inform carrier negotiations (e.g., setup fees and minimums), dock scheduling, and ESG reporting. We will review sensitivity to the management weights and operational thresholds to understand trade-offs and prepare contingency options.
